fullPassage: Born in 1888 in Bombay (now Mumbai), India, Sarojini Naidu was a talented poet and political leader. She received the nickname "The Nightingale of India" because of the beauty of her poetry. She began writing poetry at age 12 and was soon recognized for her literary talent. In 1905, her first collection of poems was published. Later she joined India's struggle for freedom from British rule. As a powerful speaker, she traveled widely and influenced many people. She became the first woman to serve as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1925. After India's independence, she served as the governor of the Uttar Pradesh province until her death in 1949.
